subject.title: fix(plugins): deep-clone registry snapshot so nested mutations roll back (#107514)

question: Should plugin registry transactions support prototype-preserving deep rollback for arbitrary plugin-provided custom instances, or restrict registry values to an explicitly supported cloneable data contract?
rationale: The patch resolves the reported shared-reference rollback failure, but its behavior for future plugin-defined object types becomes an implicit compatibility contract that tests alone cannot set permanently.

options.title: Approve the broad snapshot contract
options.body: Accept prototype-preserving recursive cloning for custom registry instances, retaining functions by reference, and merge once normal checks finish.

options.title: Narrow the supported value contract
options.body: Limit snapshot values to documented plain data, collections, Date, and callable references, then reject or normalize unsupported plugin-defined instances at registration time.

recommendation.title: Approve the broad snapshot contract
recommendation.body: Accept prototype-preserving recursive cloning for custom registry instances, retaining functions by reference, and merge once normal checks finish.

likelyOwner.reason: No path-specific current-main ownership signal was available in the supplied history, so this compatibility decision should be routed through the plugin-area reviewer assigned by maintainers.
